chunks: He is called by the kunya of Abu Ja'far and is titled Shaykh al-Ta'ifa and al-Shaykh without qualification.

key_terms.الطَّائِفَةِ: the Shia community; al-ta'ifa al-imamiyya is the technical term for the Twelver Shia
key_terms.الْإِطْلَاقِ: without qualification or restriction; in the absolute sense — denoting the uniqueness of this title for one scholar
key_terms.يُكْنَى: to be given a kunya — a patronymic honorific of the form 'Father of…'
key_terms.يُلَقَّبُ: to be given a laqab — an honorific epithet bestowed in recognition of a quality or achievement

ai.seo_question: What is the kunya and laqab of Shaykh al-Tusi in Shia scholarship?
ai.summary: This biographical notice identifies the renowned Shia jurist and hadith scholar Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi (385–460 AH / 995–1067 CE) by his patronymic (kunya) Abu Ja'far and his two honorific titles. The designation 'al-Shaykh without qualification' reflects his supreme standing: in classical Shia scholarship the unqualified term 'al-Shaykh' refers exclusively to him, just as 'al-Saduq' refers exclusively to Ibn Babawayh.
word_analysis: he is called by the kunya
